payload.reason: The evidence suggests that incorrectly-classified actions and objects can lead to ambiguity for humans, as they rely on physical relations and commonsense knowledge that may not be explicitly stated.

claims.text: Incorrectly-classified actions and objects can create ambiguity for humans due to the reliance on physical relations and commonsense knowledge.
Ambiguity arises when the physical implications of actions are not clearly understood, as shown in examples of underspecified frames.
